text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.24% today to close at $478.07, capping a volatile two-week rally of 13.2% that mirrors sharp moves in crude oil prices. The stock has tracked the oil market's response to Iran's escalating military actions in the Strait of Hormuz—world oil prices hit $126.55 per barrel as shipping threats tightened, while U.S. crude climbed toward $102 amid real concerns about regional supply disruption. Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, which means tighter margins, but higher crude and product prices have more than offset that headwind over the past two weeks.

The stock's gains also reflect the real squeeze on global refining: tanker rates are surging as vessels avoid the Hormuz route, pushing the true delivered cost of physical oil up $30–$40 per barrel above the headline price. For a major U.S. refiner like Marathon, this means stronger margins on fuel sales even if crude costs more to acquire, since refined products move at premium prices in a tight market. Today's mild move masks the underlying strength that's driven the two-week surge.
